messages:
sara: Quick sync — Acme told us they're planning a drop-in replacement for RivalAI and want a short eval to validate parity. They care about prompt/response shape, cost delta, and security questionnaire. Can we outline POC steps and blockers? :eyes:

raj: Re: prompt/response shape — their app relies on exact field ordering and a few heuristic tokens. Biggest issues historically: different tokenizer -> token counts change, stop sequence behavior varies, different default temperature/penalty settings. We should surface examples.

michael: I can own the technical POC. Plan suggestion: 1) create a small shim that maps RivalAI params -> Redwood equivalents, 2) run an automated prompt suite (50 canonical prompts + edge cases), 3) measure diffs (token count, response length, top-1 text diffs, JSON schema validity).

michael: Example shim mapping (pseudo-curl):
```
# RivalAI style call -> Redwood mapping
curl -X POST https://api.reddemo/v1/generate \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \ 
  -d '{"prompt": "{{prompt}}", "max_tokens": 256, "temperature": 0.0, "stop": ["\n\n" ] }'
```

michael: Notes: Rival's `top_p` default vs Redwood's, plus Rival sends `n=3` for multiple completions which we should canonicalize.

oliver: On pricing — Acme is worried about per-token delta and burst throughput. They'll want an apples-to-apples estimate for 1M monthly messages, 75% short prompts, 25% long. Any quick ballpark?

michael: Ballpark: hosted per-token will likely be similar for same model family; main delta is throughput (they may need Dedicated for predictable QPS). For 1M messages with average 150 tokens generated, show both hosted cost and a Dedicated reserved estimate. I'll produce numbers in the POC deck.

anya: Security questions: Acme requires SOC2, tenant isolation, key management, and an executable security questionnaire (they sent an SSAQ). We also need to confirm: do we persist request/response for hosted POCs? retention policy?

sara: They explicitly said: no retention for PII during eval unless agreed. Can we do a retention-disabled mode for the POC?

infra-bot: deploy status: created ephemeral workspace for acme-poc in staging (workspace-id: ws-acme-42). Credentials will expire in 7d.

michael: For retention: we can flip an env var for the POC to not store request/response and route logs to ephemeral storage — will require SRE sign-off.

anya: We'll need to fill their security questionnaire and include a short note about transient logs and KMS integration. I can take the questionnaire if someone drops the form in this thread.

sara: Dropped their Q via DM to @anya, also uploaded sample SSAQ link: https://acme.example/ssaq-2026.pdf

raj: Back to parity: two practical mitigations for response diffs — 1) response normalizer that enforces JSON schema & fallback behavior, 2) simulated encoder step to estimate token counts and adjust max_tokens before sending. Both can be in the shim.

michael: Agreed. Also add a prompt-surface test: compare seeds across temperature=0.0 and temp=0.2 and measure divergence. If divergence > threshold, flag for manual review.

oliver: Acme also mentioned enterprise blocker: legal wants an SLA for inference latency at 95th percentile. Can we commit during POC?

michael: We can provide staged SLOs in hosted staging and offer Dedicated as the route to guaranteed 95th pct. For the POC timeline, we'll show observed 95p numbers and a Dedicated plan for production.

sara: Proposed POC checklist (short):
- onboarding + access (infra-bot workspace)
- security questionnaire answered (anya)
- prompt suite run + diff report (michael, raj)
- pricing delta + Dedicated option (oliver)
- response normalizer sketch + sample shim (michael)
- acceptance criteria doc from Acme (sara)

anya: I'll need a contact and a copy of their data flow diagram for the SSAQ.

sara: Contact is @marie (Acme eng). I'll intro via email today.

michael: I'll start building the shim and the test harness. ETA initial results in 3 business days.

raj: I'll curate the canonical prompts and edge cases list — will post as a gist later.

oliver: I'll draft a pricing comparison spreadsheet (hosted vs Dedicated) and include throughput assumptions.

sara: Great. One more blocker they called out: some downstream parsers rely on RivalAI adding trailing commas in list outputs (lol). If we differ, their ingestion fails. We need the normalizer to optionally emulate Rival quirks.

michael: We can add a mode `--emulate-rival-quirks` to the shim. Should be explicit and gated behind POC flag.

anya: Ack. Keep me posted on any data retention toggles so I can update the SSAQ answers.

sara: Action items assigned. I'll follow up with a short status update tomorrow. :thumbsup:
